Bayesian temperature reconstructions with a second predictor

Source: R/rec.ion.bayesian.R
rec.ion.bayesian.Rd

Reconstructs temperatures (in degrees C) from the posterior draws of cal.ion.bayesian(), the measured D47, and the Ion value of each sample.

Usage

rec.ion.bayesian(
  calModel,
  recData,
  ndraws = 10000,
  useIonError = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

calModel

Posterior draws from cal.draws(), a result from cal.ion.bayesian(), or the stanfit in it.

recData

The reconstruction dataset. It needs the columns Sample, D47, D47error (1 SD of the D47 value), and Ion. Add N (number of replicates) or D47sd (SD of the replicates) to also get SD. The output of avg.replicates() has both. It also needs IonError (1 SD of Ion) when useIonError = TRUE.

ndraws

Number of draws used for each sample.

useIonError

Whether to account for the error in Ion.

level

Probability covered by the interval.

...

Arguments from earlier versions (iter, postcalsamples, and MC). They are ignored.

Value

A data.frame with one row per sample. meanTemp is the posterior mean temperature (in degrees C). SE is the standard error of the temperature, propagated from D47error. SD is the SD of the temperature of a single replicate, propagated from the SD of the replicates (D47error x sqrt(N), or D47sd when N is missing). It is NA without replicate information. Both include the uncertainty in the calibration. median, lower, and upper are the posterior median and the limits of the interval, based on SE.

Details

With flat priors on 10^6/T^2 and Ion, the posterior of Ion follows its measurement, and the posterior of 10^6/T^2 for each draw is normal. Both are sampled directly, so no MCMC run is needed. Draws with 10^6/T^2 at or below zero are not physically possible. They are removed with a warning.

The uncertainty includes the calibration parameters, the residual SD of the calibration (sigma), D47error, and IonError when used.

Examples

# \donttest{
ds <- cal.dataset(error = "S1", nobs = 50, seed = 1)
ds$Ion <- rnorm(nrow(ds))
fit <- cal.ion.bayesian(ds, IonError = 0.1, numSavedSteps = 1000)
#> Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)): error in evaluating the argument 'object' in selecting a method for function 'sampling': Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')
recData <- data.frame(Sample = "A", D47 = 0.6, D47error = 0.01, Ion = 0, IonError = 0.1)
rec.ion.bayesian(fit, recData, useIonError = TRUE)
#> Error: object 'fit' not found
# }
